newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil stable in thin market.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil stable in thin market.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel prices were stable on Tuesday with little buying interest for anything but Russian cargo.
Offers for low sulphur straight-run were heard around $105 and $106 fob NWE. No buying was seen although trans- Atlantic interest was indicated.
Russian material was reported to be available occasionally with the post-winter flood not yet apparent.
"Its not a very active market, the Russians are coming up sporadically and everything goes very quickly," said one trader.
E-4 premiums of from $3 to $5 were being discussed, with levels hard to pin down, traders said. One cargo of M-40 with a high water content was heard traded on Monday but details were unavailable.
At least one Black Sea cargo was heard being offered in the Mediterranean area. It added to good supply of material in the region, though of diverse quality.
Three cargoes of Libyan material loaded at the weekend but their destinations were unclear. A cargo of Tunisian straight-run is being offered by tender to load 6-8 April.
